answer: The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, published publicly on failure, each submission carries a fresh nonce. Each submission hangs on the ferrous of a task receipt, and the atlas is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Reaching the anchor of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work.
